title: Cultures and Festivals
description: Celebrations and traditions around the world.

entries.title: Eid
entries.summary: Eid is a happy time for Muslims around the world.
entries.body: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of the month of Ramadan, when people fast from dawn to sunset. Families come together, new clothes are worn, and food is shared. Eid al-Adha is the Festival of Sacrifice.
facts: Families visit each other and give gifts.
Eid al-Adha is also called the Festival of Sacrifice.

entries.title: Christmas
entries.body: Many families in Christian countries celebrate Christmas with a decorated tree, gifts and a special meal. For Christians, Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus. In some countries Santa Claus brings the presents.
facts: Christmas Day is the 25th of December.
The Christmas tree is a tradition from Germany.
Christmas is a religious and also a family celebration.

entries.title: Diwali
entries.summary: Diwali is the festival of lights in India.
entries.body: Diwali is celebrated by Hindus around the world. Houses are cleaned and decorated with lamps, and fireworks are lit. The festival celebrates good winning over evil, and light winning over darkness.
facts: Diwali means a row of lamps.
It is celebrated in the autumn, often in October or November.
People wear new clothes and share sweets.

entries.title: New Year
entries.summary: Many countries welcome the new year with a count down.
entries.body: When the clock strikes midnight on the last night of the year, people often shout 'Happy New Year'. In Japan people clean their houses and visit the temple at the start of the year. In many places fireworks are set off.
facts: The count down happens at midnight on 31 December.
In Japan, people visit a temple at the start of the year.
Fireworks are a traditional part of New Year celebrations.

entries.title: UAE National Day
entries.summary: The UAE celebrates its national day on 2 December.
entries.body: On 2 December the UAE remembers the day the seven emirates joined together in 1971. People decorate their cars and homes with flags, and there are parades, music and food.
facts: National Day is on the 2nd of December.
It marks the union of the seven emirates in 1971.
Cars and homes are decorated with flags.

entries.title: Traditions
entries.summary: Traditions are customs that are passed down.
entries.body: A tradition is something a family or community does again and again, like welcoming guests with tea or dressing up for a festival. Traditions change a little over time, and they can be different in every country.
facts: Traditions are customs passed down through generations.
Food, clothes and greetings are all part of traditions.
Every country and family has its own traditions.
